title: Heliacal 3/8: object location & magnitude layer (Ephemeris-consuming helpers)
description:
### Summary
Port swehel.c's ephemeris-consuming helper layer: SunRA, ObjectLoc, azalt_cart, Magnitude, and the rise/set wrappers (calc_rise_and_set, my_rise_trans, RiseSet). These take `eph: &Ephemeris` plus explicit dgeo/datm and route through the existing stateless API (`calc_ut_with_config`, `pheno_ut`, `fixstar2_mag`, `rise_trans`, `azalt`) — never a backend.

Read docs/codebase-map.md first. Do NOT read ../swisseph C source — the ref doc is the source of truth. Stateless: C's static caches here (SunRA's tjdlast/ralast) are pure memoization — drop them, recompute.

### Files
- `src/heliacal.rs` — append after the brightness layer (order in file: helpers may precede if you prefer; keep one coherent section with a `// --- object location & magnitude (c-ref-heliacal-vision.md §7) ---` header).
- `tests/c-gen/gen_heliacal_internals.c` — extend with `"objectloc"` and `"magnitude"` batteries; regenerate JSON.
- `tests/golden/heliacal_internals.rs` — extend.

### Implementation steps
1. `sun_ra(eph, jd_ut) -> f64` per docs/c-ref-heliacal-vision.md §7: the SHIPPED code path is the SIMULATE_VICTORVB calendar approximation — `swe_revjul` to get month/day, then `degnorm((month + (day-1)/30.4 - 3.69) * 30)`. The swe_calc-based branch is DEAD (vision §11) — do not port it. It ignores HIGH_PRECISION and ΔT by design. Use `crate::date` for revjul.
2. Flag plumbing per vision §2: the C `helflag` carries SEFLG ephemeris bits in its low bits. Rust design (decided): heliacal functions take `epheflag: CalcFlags` + `helflag: HeliacalFlags` separately (the rise_trans/context.rs idiom). Wherever the ref doc says `iflag = helflag & SEFLG_EPHMASK`, use `epheflag & calc::EPHMASK`. Where C calls `swe_set_topo(dgeo)` + TOPOCTR, use the riseset.rs `topo_config` pattern: clone `eph.config`, set `.topographic` from dgeo, call `eph.calc_ut_with_config(...)` with TOPOCTR. Follow §2/§7 exactly on which call sites set TOPOCTR and which don't.
3. `object_loc(eph, jd_ut, dgeo, datm, object_name, angle, epheflag, helflag) -> Result<f64, Error>` per §7 — the Angle selector table (§7 lists the meanings: azimuth/topo-alt/app-alt/RA/decl etc.); planet vs fixed-star dispatch via `object_to_body` from 1/8. PORT LITERALLY the Angle==4 branch's argument order quirk: it passes `(xaz[1], datm[0], datm[1], ...)` to AppAltfromTopoAlt — pressure/temperature swapped relative to every other call site (vision §7 flags this). Golden parity requires reproducing it.
4. `azalt_cart` per §7 (cartesian az/alt variant used by pheno later).
5. `magnitude(eph, jd_ut, dgeo, object_name, epheflag, helflag) -> Result<f64, Error>` per §7: planets → `eph.pheno_ut(...)` apparent-magnitude slot; fixed stars → `eph.fixstar2_mag(name)`. `fast_magnitude` is DEAD (vision §11) — skip.
6. Rise/set wrappers per §7: `calc_rise_and_set`, `my_rise_trans`, `rise_set` (C RiseSet) — route through `Ephemeris::rise_trans` / `rise_trans_true_hor` with the rsmi bits §7 specifies (DISC_CENTER/BIT_NO_REFRACTION handling, the Rim parameter, twilight bits). Note §7's AU literal quirk in calc_rise_and_set if flagged (a different AU constant than riseset's) — keep it local to heliacal, do not "fix" to constants::AUNIT.
7. Extend gen_heliacal_internals.c: `"objectloc"` — ObjectLoc for objects {"venus","sirius","moon"} × every Angle value in §7's table × jd_ut {2451545.0, 2453371.0} × Cairo dgeo [31.25, 30.1, 30.0] × datm [1013.25,15,40,40] × helflag SEFLG_SWIEPH; `"magnitude"` — same objects × both epochs. C side: `swe_set_ephe_path("../../swisseph/ephe")` (relative from tests/c-gen, copy gen_eclipse.c's handling; star-name buffers must be `char[]` locals, not string literals — swe_fixstar strcpy's in place, see gen_eclipse.c's comment). Rust side: build the Ephemeris like tests/golden/eclipse.rs's `make_eph()` (ephe_path set so Sirius resolves).
8. Regenerate JSON; extend tests/golden/heliacal_internals.rs. Tolerances: ObjectLoc angles eps 1e-7 (compounds azalt/sidtime like the azalt golden battery); magnitudes eps 1e-8.

### C reference
docs/c-ref-heliacal-vision.md §2, §7, §11.

### Golden tests
- Same harness build/run as 1/8 and 2/8.
- `cargo test --test golden heliacal_internals -- --nocapture`.

### Acceptance criteria
- `cargo test --test golden heliacal_internals -- --nocapture` passes (all batteries incl. 1/8, 2/8).
- `cargo test` full suite green; no new clippy warnings.

### Escape hatch
If golden tests fail with errors > 1e-8 (angles: > 1e-6) after two debugging attempts, STOP and report failing cases, actual vs expected, what you tried. Escalate to Opus.
execution_record: Implemented all functions from the plan: sun_ra (crude calendar approximation), object_loc (7-angle accessor), azalt_cart (cartesian variant), magnitude (pheno_ut for planets, fixstar2_mag for stars), calc_rise_and_set (fast Newton rise/set), my_rise_trans (dispatcher), rise_set (wrapper). Added pheno_with_config/pheno_ut_with_config to phenomena.rs for threading topographic config through magnitude. Initial golden test failure (6.7e-6 objectloc, 2.4e-7 magnitude) was caused by the test Ephemeris using Moshier (Default) while C generated data with SEFLG_SWIEPH — fixed by setting ephemeris_source: Swiss in make_eph(). All 137 tests pass, no new clippy warnings.

messages.text: Review: approve with notes. Object location & magnitude layer golden-verified (objectloc 42 cases @ 1e-7, magnitude 6 cases @ 1e-8). One high finding: azalt_cart multiplies by DEGTORAD before polar_to_cartesian, but C feeds raw degrees to swi_polcart (which expects radians) — a C quirk that must be reproduced for golden parity. Will cause failures in task 107 (VisLimMagn) if not fixed. One low finding: pheno_ut should delegate to pheno_ut_with_config to avoid fallback-logic duplication.
